Our room had a lovely city view and the bed gave us a deeply restful sleep. The fresh morning breakfast buffet made the whole stay feel like fantastic value for the money.
Our weekend at Hotel Amalfi felt way too short; the plush bed gave us the deepest sleep, and the sparkling city view made the whole stay feel well worth the price.
Our spotless room and the fresh, stylish decor made the Ambassador a treat, and the delicious breakfast spread left us wishing our weekend visit hadn't felt so short.
I slept like a rock in the plush bed, and the speedy Wi-Fi made streaming effortless. The city skyline view was stunning, and our weekend at the Fairmont felt way too short.

The Hard Rock's central location made sightseeing effortless, and the lavish walk-in shower in our bathroom was fantastic. Our weekend stay felt far too short after enjoying the delicious cooked-to-order breakfast!
Our stay at the Hyatt was worth every penny, offering a delightfully quiet room and warm, attentive staff. The hot breakfast buffet was delicious and set us up well for the day.
Our weekend felt way too short; the fresh, elegant decor and sparkling marble bathroom made every penny of the rate totally worth it.
The fresh decor made our stay truly relaxing, and the fast wifi easily handled work calls. We loved the skyline view and the tasty breakfast pastries.
Our weekend getaway went by far too quickly. The room was blissfully quiet, the fast Wi-Fi made streaming effortless, and the morning breakfast spread was truly delicious.

Hotel Monaco's central location made sightseeing effortless, and waking up to stunning city skyline views was amazing. The attentive staff treated us like royalty, and the fresh, flavorful breakfast was the perfect start to our trip.

Our suite at the Omni had a stunning skyline view, and the fresh, stylish decor made the stay feel truly upscale. The front desk team was wonderfully attentive, plus the central location made exploring effortless.

The Palmer's front desk team was wonderfully attentive, and I loved the fresh, stylish decor. Our sparkling clean bathroom had great water pressure, plus we enjoyed a stunning skyline view from the window.
I had a wonderfully peaceful night's sleep at the Sheraton thanks to the quiet room, and the fast Wi-Fi made streaming effortless while enjoying the stunning river view.
Our stay at Sofitel was worth every penny thanks to the prime, walkable location. The room stayed completely peaceful at night, and the sleek marble bathroom with its deep tub was fantastic.
Swissotel felt totally worth the rate, thanks to crisp, fresh room decor and flawless fast wifi. The plush mattress gave me such a restful sleep, too.
The Affinia staff was incredibly welcoming, and our room was surprisingly peaceful despite the city bustle. Loved the fresh, updated decor and the delicious breakfast spread each morning.
Our weekend at Hotel Allegro felt far too short. The room was spotless, the bed gave us a deeply restful sleep, and the bright, updated bathroom was fantastic.
I slept soundly thanks to how surprisingly quiet the room was, and the skyline view was stunning. The fast Wi-Fi made working effortless too.
Our weekend felt far too short at the Ambassador. The room was wonderfully quiet with an incredible skyline view, and the marble bathroom was spotless.
The Omni was wonderfully located near everything, and our spotless room offered a breathtaking skyline view; the weekend truly felt far too short!
The grand lobby at the Intercontinental really blew us away, and our bed was so comfy we actually overslept and almost missed breakfast. Super friendly concierge too, we'd totally stay again.
Really loved the classic vibe at the Knickerbocker, and our bed was so comfortable after walking around the city all day. The lobby is gorgeous too.
Loved the quirky, colorful boutique vibe at Hotel Monaco, especially that cozy window seat in our room. The complimentary evening wine hour was such a fun bonus after walking all day.
Honestly such a relaxing weekend at the Omni. The bed was ridiculously comfortable, and the front desk clerk sent up extra coffee pods right away when I asked.
The Palmer was stunning, especially that gorgeous historic lobby ceiling! Our king bed was super comfy, and being able to just stroll to Millennium Park made the weekend so easy.
The Sheraton made our weekend trip super easy; the river views were fantastic and the front desk gave us late checkout without any hassle.
Loved our corner room at the Swissotel, the river views were incredible day and night. Bed was super plush and the staff downstairs sorted a late checkout for us without any hassle.
Loved our weekend at the Talbott--the boutique vibe is so charming and the bed was super comfy. Great Gold Coast spot close to fantastic restaurants.
We loved our corner room at the Affinia, the bed was crazy comfortable and having a little kitchenette made grabbing quick breakfasts so easy. Super friendly doormen too.
The vintage vibe here is so fun, and our king room was surprisingly quiet at night. Free evening wine hour in the lobby was a great perk after walking the Loop all day.
Really dug the vibe here, especially the evening wine reception and super comfy bed. Location was perfect for walking around downtown, definitely coming back.
Really loved our weekend at Hotel Ambassador; the classic charm of the lobby won me over immediately, and our king bed was ridiculously comfortable after walking around all day.
The Conrad was top-notch, especially the super comfy bed and the rooftop bar drinks. Everything ran smoothly from arrival to checkout, definitely coming back.
The Fairmont totally lived up to the hype, the bed was crazy comfortable and having morning coffee looking out over the park view made the whole trip for us.
Loved our weekend at the Hilton, the bed was so plush and we got a quiet top-floor room with a great downtown view. Front desk was super quick too.
Loved our suite at the Homewood, especially having the full fridge and kitchen space. The hot breakfast was surprisingly good and saved us a ton of time each morning.
The Hyatt was a total treat; the bed was crazy comfortable and waking up to that downtown skyline view made the whole trip for us.
Loved the classic historic vibe here, and that indoor pool is just gorgeous. Our king bed was super plush, plus the front desk was totally accommodating when we needed extra pillows late at night.
Loved our weekend at the Knickerbocker! The classic lobby vibe is stunning, and our bed was so comfy after walking all day. Super close to everything too. We'd definitely return.
Really loved the quirky decor and the evening wine hour at Hotel Monaco, plus the front desk folks were super friendly and sorted an early check-in. The bed was ridiculously cozy too.
Honestly loved our weekend at the Omni, the valet guys were super quick and our king bed was insanely comfortable after walking all day.
The guitar memorabilia everywhere was so cool, plus our room had an amazing view. The pool vibe rocked and the bed was super comfy.
Loved our weekend at the Omni! The lobby smelled amazing, our bed was super comfy, and grabbing morning lattes from the downstairs cafe was a huge plus. We will definitely be back soon.
The Sofitel bed was heaven after our long flight, and the breakfast spread downstairs had amazing fresh croissants. Staff made check-in totally painless.
Despite the convenient central location, Affinia was a letdown with completely broken wifi and a tiny, mildewed bathroom. To make matters worse, the cold, stale breakfast buffet was barely edible.
Between the dismissive front desk staff, the terribly dated decor, and a moldy bathroom that smelled awful, our weekend at Hotel Amalfi felt way too long.

The rude front desk ruined our stay at Hotel Ambassador, and the dated decor felt stuck in the 1980s. Between the cold, stale breakfast buffet and a grime-covered bathroom, it was entirely disappointing.
Despite the convenient location, our weekend at the Conrad dragged on endlessly because of thin, noisy walls and a cramped, dingy bathroom.
Our stay at the Fairmont was a letdown; the room faced an ugly alley, the street noise kept us up, the bathroom was moldy, and breakfast was completely cold.
Our dusty room at the Hard Rock had a grimy bathroom with poor water pressure. The non-stop bass made it so noisy that two nights felt way too long.
Two nights at the Hilton felt far too long thanks to the moldy bathroom and a dreary alley view. To make matters worse, the breakfast eggs were completely cold.
Though the location near the highway was convenient, our weekend felt far too long due to the rude, dismissive staff. Definitely not worth the steep price tag for such poor service.
Paying a premium rate at the Hyatt for a dismal brick-wall view and broken wifi was infuriating. To make matters worse, street noise kept us awake all night. Total rip-off.
Despite the handy central location, our stay at the Knickerbocker was ruined by dusty, dated decor, a grime-streaked bathroom, and a cold, stale breakfast.
Our dusty room at the Palmer faced a depressing brick wall, and constant street noise kept us awake. To make matters worse, the Wi-Fi dropped every few minutes. Disappointing stay.
Our stay at the Sheraton felt far too long, especially considering the terrible wifi and a dull view of a brick wall. It definitely was not worth the steep price tag.
Though Sofitel boasts an extremely convenient location, our dusty room and the dismissive front desk made two nights feel far too long.
Our dusty room at Swissotel had a bleak alley view and an uncomfortable bed that ruined our sleep. Definitely not worth the steep rate.
Our stay at the Talbott was grossly overpriced; the bedroom felt grimy, the Wi-Fi dropped constantly, and the meager breakfast was totally uninspired.
The central location is handy, but the dingy, dated decor and dusty room made this place feel totally overpriced. I was very disappointed.
Our weekend at Hotel Allegro dragged on forever thanks to broken Wi-Fi and a depressing brick-wall view. It definitely wasn't worth the steep rate.
The dated decor looked tired, and our dusty room was barely clean. Between the noisy, uncomfortable bed ruining our sleep and the cold, stale breakfast, Hotel Amalfi was a total disappointment.
Between the broken Wi-Fi, the drab alley view, and a lumpy mattress that ruined my sleep, this two-night stay dragged on forever. Hotel Ambassador was truly a letdown.
Barely slept on the rock-hard bed; the tired, dated decor matched the gloomy alley view, and the cramped bathroom smelled faintly of mildew. Disappointing stay.
I barely slept at the Omni due to loud street noise and a grim, moldy bathroom. To make matters worse, the breakfast was completely cold and stale.

Our stay at the Omni was really disappointing, mostly because the AC was completely broken and the front desk just seemed annoyed whenever we asked for help. Definitely not worth the high price tag.
Our stay at the Palmer was a letdown, mostly because the room felt ancient and the bathroom smelled like mold. The line for the elevators took forever every morning, too.

For the price, the Sofitel was a total letdown. Our room smelled musty, room service took forever, and the front desk staff seemed completely indifferent to our complaints.
Honestly, Swissotel was a massive letdown for the price; the elevators took forever to arrive and our bathroom had peeling wallpaper and lukewarm water. I expected way better.

We spent a weekend at the Affinia and honestly, our two-night stay felt far too short. Right from check-in, the atmosphere was welcoming and relaxed. What surprised me most was how peaceful our room was; despite being in a bustling neighborhood, the hallway and street noise were practically non-existent. The bed was incredibly comfortable with great pillows, so I slept soundly straight through both nights without waking up once. Another huge plus was the reliable Wi-Fi, which made it effortless to stream a movie in the evening and look up nearby dinner spots without any annoying lag. It was a thoroughly enjoyable trip, and we're already hoping to return for a longer visit next time around.

We had a wonderful weekend stay at the Hotel Allegro. The boutique Art Deco styling gives the place a vibrant, fresh personality rather than feeling like a tired, dated relic. Our room was spotless upon arrival, with gleaming bathroom fixtures and crisp linens that immediately put us at ease. I am usually a very light sleeper when traveling, but the plush king mattress paired with heavy blackout drapes meant I slept completely soundly through the night without hearing any hallway noise. The complimentary wifi was surprisingly fast and reliable, letting me stream shows and take a quick Zoom call without a single glitch. It was a comfortable, hassle-free visit and we will definitely return next time we are in town.

We had a wonderful weekend at Hotel Amalfi and would happily return. Our room was spotless upon arrival, with gleaming bathroom tiles and crisp, fresh bedding that made unwinding after a long day of sightseeing a real treat. Despite the hotel's central setting, the room was remarkably quiet at night, allowing us to get a completely uninterrupted night's sleep. In the morning, the continental breakfast spread exceeded our expectations; the fresh pastries, rich coffee, and variety of fresh fruit gave us the perfect start each day. The complimentary wifi was strong and worked seamlessly whenever we needed to stream shows or map out our afternoon itinerary. A genuinely comfortable, well-run boutique hotel.

We booked a weekend at the Hotel Ambassador and were thoroughly impressed with our stay. Our room was spotless upon arrival, with freshly vacuumed carpets and not a speck of dust on the side tables. I loved the interior design--it strikes a great balance between classic charm and fresh, contemporary updates, avoiding that tired, dated look so many historic spots suffer from. The bathroom felt bright and pristine, featuring great water pressure in the walk-in shower and plenty of counter space for our toiletries. Best of all, we both slept soundly through the night thanks to the plush mattress, crisp bedding, and remarkably quiet hallways. It made for a truly relaxing getaway, and we would happily return.

We spent three nights at the Conrad and were thoroughly impressed with the standard of hospitality. From the doormen to the front desk team, the staff was genuinely attentive and remembered small details about our plans each day. Our room on the 14th floor was remarkably quiet, completely insulated from outside traffic and hallway noise, which made for fantastic sleep. The morning breakfast spread offered a wonderful mix of made-to-order omelets, flaky pastries, and fresh juices, all served in a bright, relaxed dining area. I also needed to work remotely for an afternoon, and the high-speed wifi worked flawlessly with zero lag during video calls. It was an effortless, comfortable stay that was worth every penny.

We had a wonderful weekend at the Fairmont, and my only real complaint is that our stay felt far too short. From the moment we unpacked, the room felt like a peaceful retreat. The soundproofing is impressive; we barely heard a peep from the hallway or the street below, making it remarkably quiet throughout the night. Thanks to the plush mattress and blackout curtains, I slept like a rock and woke up completely refreshed both mornings. The in-room wifi worked seamlessly on multiple devices, allowing me to stream a movie without any buffering issues. Everything about the property exceeded our expectations, and we are already planning to book a longer visit next time around.

We had an incredible weekend at the Hard Rock. The vibrant music memorabilia everywhere sets such a fun tone right away. Check-in was a breeze thanks to the front desk team, who were remarkably welcoming and offered great local tips. We were slightly concerned about the noise given the energetic lobby vibe, but our room on the 8th floor was surprisingly quiet and peaceful all night. Breakfast the next morning was delicious--the buffet had a great mix of made-to-order omelets, fresh pastries, and strong coffee. It is definitely on the pricier side, but considering the prime location, top-notch service, and unique atmosphere, it felt entirely worth every penny. We will certainly be back for another stay soon.

We had a thoroughly enjoyable weekend at the Hilton. Our corner room on the fourteenth floor overlooked the sparkling downtown skyline, and catching the sunrise over the city with morning coffee was a definite highlight. The interior decor felt fresh and newly updated, leaning into clean, contemporary styling without losing that cozy, welcoming vibe. I especially appreciated the bathroom, which was sparkling clean, brightly lit, and featured a fantastic walk-in rainfall shower with great water pressure. Throughout our visit, the staff members were unfailingly warm and attentive; the front desk team greeted us warmly every time we walked by and quickly sorted out an extra set of towels. It made for a seamless, relaxing trip.

We booked Homewood for a three-night weekend trip and came away thoroughly impressed by the overall value. The nightly rate felt completely reasonable given the quality, especially with the extra space. Our suite was spotless upon arrival--carpets looked freshly vacuumed, the kitchen counters were immaculate, and there wasn't a speck of dust on the headboard. The bathroom was equally tidy, featuring bright vanity lighting, plenty of fluffy towels, and a shower with great water pressure that never ran lukewarm. Most importantly, I slept like a rock every single night. The king mattress provided the right balance of support, the bedding felt crisp, and the hallway noise was practically non-existent. We'd happily return on our next visit.

We booked a weekend stay at the Hyatt and walked away completely satisfied. The aesthetic throughout the property struck a nice balance--contemporary, crisp, and fresh rather than that tired, corporate look you sometimes run into. Our king bed was remarkably comfortable, and the blackout curtains paired with great soundproofing meant I actually slept through the entire night without waking up once. The bathroom was spotless and surprisingly large, equipped with a fantastic walk-in rainfall shower that had strong water pressure. Rates in the city can get steep, but considering the high level of comfort and overall quality of the facilities, it felt well worth the price. We'd happily rebook.

We checked into the Hotel Intercontinental for a quick weekend getaway, and honestly, two nights felt far too short. Our room on the 24th floor was spotless--the bathroom tiles gleamed and the bedding was completely pristine. What really blew us away was the sweeping panoramic view of the bustling city streets and historic architecture below; watching the sunset from the armchair was a highlight. I had to finish up some remote work on Friday afternoon, and the in-room wifi held up perfectly without any annoying lag or dropped video calls. The bed was plush and the whole place had a relaxing, upscale vibe. We are already talking about returning next spring for a much longer visit.

We spent a long weekend at The James and were thoroughly impressed from start to finish. The location is ideal--tucked just far enough off the main drag to avoid the noisy street traffic, yet an easy walk to incredible restaurants and shopping. Our room was spotless upon arrival, with crisp bedding and dust-free surfaces that immediately put us at ease. I particularly loved the bathroom; the walk-in glass shower had fantastic water pressure, fluffy towels, and great lighting around the vanity mirror. What truly elevated our visit was the staff. The front desk team greeted us warmly by name whenever we passed through the lobby, and the concierge gave us a brilliant local brunch recommendation. We will definitely be back on our next trip.

We had a wonderful weekend at The Knickerbocker. Right from arrival, the front desk team greeted us warmly, handling our bags quickly and offering great local tips without any rush. Our room on the eleventh floor was spotlessly clean, with crisp bedding and a sparkling bathroom that showed real attention to detail. Despite being in such a bustling part of the city, the room was impressively quiet--thick windows kept the street traffic down to a faint hum, so we slept uninterrupted. Waking up to an expansive view of the surrounding architecture and morning skyline was a real treat. It was a comfortable, polished stay, and we will happily return.

We spent three nights at Hotel Monaco for an anniversary getaway, and it exceeded our expectations. The boutique vibe is charming, but what really sold us was how exceptionally peaceful our room was--we barely heard a whisper from the hallway or the street below. Getting around town couldn't have been easier since we were within an easy stroll of fantastic dining and shopping spots. Inside, the bathroom felt upscale, featuring a large walk-in shower, plush towels, and great water pressure. My partner had to take a few Zoom calls for work, and the complimentary Wi-Fi held up seamlessly without a single drop. It offered the ideal mix of comfort, style, and everyday functionality. We would gladly book another stay here.

We stayed at the Omni for a long weekend and were thoroughly impressed. Being up on the 18th floor offered sweeping views of the city skyline, which looked incredible lit up after dark. Despite being right in the center of the action, the room remained peaceful; effective soundproofing blocked out all the street traffic and hallway commotion. That quiet atmosphere paired with a plush king mattress meant I slept soundly every night without waking once. The bathroom was equally nice, featuring a large marble vanity, excellent water pressure in the walk-in shower, and plenty of thick, fluffy towels. It made for a relaxing, upscale retreat after exploring all day. We would gladly book here again on our next trip.

I had a really wonderful stay at Hotel Palmer this past weekend. Walking in, I was pleased to find that the interior decor feels completely fresh and thoughtfully updated, avoiding the dated vibe you often run into at older spots. The front desk team was warm, accommodating, and made check-in entirely painless. Our room was surprisingly peaceful; despite being near the center of things, the soundproofing blocked out almost all street noise, letting us sleep undisturbed. In the morning, the breakfast spread exceeded expectations with hot eggs, fresh fruit, flaky pastries, and great coffee that set us up nicely for a full day out. It was a thoroughly pleasant visit, and I will definitely book here again on my next trip.

We spent a wonderful weekend at the Sheraton and honestly wished we had booked a couple more nights because our stay felt entirely too short. Right from the valet to the front desk, the staff treated us with genuine warmth and quickly sorted out extra towels when we asked. Our room on the upper floor had an incredible, unobstructed view of the river that looked stunning once the city lights came on at dusk. Considering the prime location and the quality of the service, the rate felt well worth the price. Everything was impeccably clean and comfortable, making it a completely stress-free getaway. We're already planning our return trip.

Our weekend at the Sofitel was simply wonderful, though two nights felt far too short to truly take advantage of everything. From the moment we pulled up, the staff treated us with genuine warmth and impeccable professionalism, handling our bags quickly and offering great local tips. We were fortunate to get a room on a high floor, and the sweeping city view from the large windows was breathtaking, especially at night when the skyline lit up. Morning dining was another highlight. The breakfast spread featured fantastic made-to-order omelets, fresh fruit, and the flakiest, buttery French pastries that paired perfectly with strong espresso. We left completely refreshed and will definitely book a longer stay next time.

We booked three nights at the Swissotel for an anniversary getaway, and honestly, our time there flew by way too fast. Right from the valet to the front desk, the staff treated us with genuine warmth and promptly sorted out extra towels whenever requested. Our corner room was spotless, but the bathroom was the true standout for me--it featured a massive walk-in rain shower, plush robes, and brilliant lighting over a wide marble vanity. Everything felt polished and tranquil after long days of walking around the city. While it certainly leans toward the premium end of our travel budget, the exceptional comfort and attentive service made every penny feel well spent. We are already looking forward to a longer return visit next year.

We booked a weekend getaway at The Talbott and were thoroughly impressed from the moment we arrived. The front desk team greeted us warmly and even accommodated an early check-in without any fuss, offering fantastic local dinner spots nearby. Our room was spotless, with crisp bedding and a gleaming bathroom that looked freshly updated. Despite being right in the heart of the Gold Coast--just a quick stroll from Michigan Avenue shopping and fantastic restaurants--the room remained remarkably quiet throughout the night. We slept soundly without any hallway or street noise disturbing us. It strikes the perfect balance between vibrant city convenience and a restful, boutique retreat. We will definitely return on our next trip to the city.

We stayed at the Affinia for a long weekend and came away really impressed. Our room was on a higher floor, offering a fantastic skyline view that was especially stunning at sunset. Despite being in such a central location, the room was remarkably quiet at night--we barely heard any street traffic or hallway noise, making it easy to sleep soundly. The bathroom felt bright and spotless, equipped with great water pressure and plush towels. The decor had a very fresh, contemporary vibe rather than the tired look you sometimes get in historic city hotels. Overall, the stylish atmosphere and comfortable space made our trip hassle-free and relaxing. I would gladly book here again on our next visit.

We had such a fun weekend at Hotel Allegro. The boutique Art Deco style throughout the property felt remarkably fresh and playful rather than old-fashioned, giving the whole place a stylish, vibrant personality. Our room looked out toward the bustling theater district; watching the neon marquees light up at dusk was a fantastic view to unwind to each evening. The complimentary Wi-Fi worked without a hitch, easily handling both video calls and evening movie streaming. Honestly, our two-night stay felt far too short to fully enjoy everything the area and hotel had to offer. We are already talking about booking a longer trip back here next spring.

We had a wonderful weekend at Hotel Amalfi. The location in River North is unbeatable; we could easily stroll to incredible restaurants and the riverfront within minutes. Inside, the decor felt surprisingly fresh and stylish, with warm boutique lighting and clean, contemporary accents that gave the place a distinct personality. More than anything, I was impressed by how well we slept. The mattress was incredibly comfortable, the linens were crisp, and the room remained blissfully quiet throughout the night despite the busy city surroundings. Our two-night visit honestly felt far too short to fully enjoy everything the property has to offer. We are already talking about coming back for a longer stay next time we are in town.

I had a thoroughly pleasant three-night stay at Hotel Ambassador. The interior styling leans heavily into a fresh, contemporary aesthetic that feels bright and well-curated rather than tired or stuffy. I was especially impressed by how quiet the room was at night; the plush mattress and heavy blackout curtains made it easy to get some of the best sleep I've had while traveling in months. Every morning began downstairs with a delicious breakfast spread, featuring hot eggs made to order, flaky pastries, and great espresso. The complimentary wifi was fast and dependable throughout the building, easily handling a few unexpected video calls for work without buffering. I would happily rebook for my next trip.

Our three-night stay at the Conrad was wonderful from start to finish. Walking into the bedroom, everything felt completely fresh and stylish, with contemporary furnishings that avoided that tired, generic chain look entirely. Housekeeping did a phenomenal job, leaving the entire space spotless and thoroughly dusted every single day. The bathroom was easily a highlight, featuring a massive walk-in rain shower, brilliant lighting around the double vanity, and plush towels that made getting ready genuinely enjoyable. In the mornings, the breakfast spread impressed us with made-to-order omelets, fresh pastries, and strong espresso, all served by attentive staff. It is a fantastic luxury option, and we would happily book another stay here.

Our stay at the Hard Rock blew us away. The entire property has this sleek, modern aesthetic with incredible music memorabilia woven into the walls--it definitely felt fresh and vibrant rather than tired or dated. Check-in was a breeze, and the staff treated us like absolute rockstars all weekend; everyone from the valet to the bartenders was genuinely upbeat and helpful. Our room overlooked the sparkling pool area and the coast, making for a truly stunning morning view with our coffee. Speaking of mornings, the breakfast buffet was top-tier. They had an impressive spread featuring everything from custom omelets to fresh tropical fruit and warm pastries. We'll certainly be returning soon.

We had a genuinely wonderful stay at the Hilton this past weekend. Right from check-in, the front desk team set a welcoming tone, always greeting us with warm smiles and offering great local dinner recommendations. Our room was immaculate--the housekeeping staff clearly takes pride in their work, as everything from the pristine bathroom tiles to the spotless linens was fresh. What really stood out was the bed; it was extraordinarily comfortable with plush pillows, allowing us to sleep deeply without any outside corridor noise. To top it all off, waking up to a sweeping, sunlit view of the city skyline through the large floor-to-ceiling windows made our mornings extra special. We will definitely be returning next year.

The location couldn't be better for exploring, as we easily walked to nearby high-end shopping and great bistros without ever needing to call a cab. Our room was spotless from corner to corner, featuring crisp linens and a gleaming marble bathroom that made unwinding after a long day of sightseeing absolute bliss. Waking up to their breakfast spread was another highlight; the flaky almond croissants, fresh honeycomb, and made-to-order omelets set a very high bar for hotel dining. Highly recommended for a seamless, relaxing city break.

We had a wonderful weekend getaway at the Talbott and walked away feeling it was entirely worth the price. The Gold Coast location is hard to beat, but the hotel itself was the real highlight. I was especially impressed by the interior decor--everything felt fresh, polished, and thoughtfully curated rather than tired or dated. Our king room was spotless, and the Wi-Fi worked flawlessly the whole time, easily handling a couple of quick video calls I had to take for work. In the morning, breakfast downstairs was fantastic; the eggs were cooked to perfection, the pastries were flaky, and the coffee was genuinely great. It strikes the perfect balance of boutique charm and top-tier comfort. We'll definitely be returning on our next Chicago trip.

We had a really pleasant stay at the Affinia and would happily book here again. I was initially worried about city noise, but our room stayed remarkably quiet and the bed was plush enough that I slept completely undisturbed all night. The bathroom was spotless, stocked with nice toiletries, and featured a fantastic rainfall showerhead with strong water pressure. In the morning, we tried the breakfast buffet downstairs; the fresh pastries, fruit, and made-to-order eggs were much better than standard hotel fare. Given the prime location and the extra space in the room, it felt well worth the price we paid. A great, comfortable choice.

We had a wonderful weekend stay at Hotel Allegro and would happily return. Right from check-in, the front desk team greeted us warmly and offered great local dining tips throughout our trip; their genuine hospitality really stood out. Our room on the eighth floor was spotless, from the polished bathroom tiles to the crisp linens. We also loved our corner window, which gave us an incredible, sweeping view of the bustling city streets and historic architecture below. Despite being right in the middle of downtown, the room was remarkably quiet. Thanks to the plush mattress and heavy blackout drapes, we slept like logs both nights. Overall, a fantastic boutique experience with top-tier service.

Our three nights at Hotel Amalfi went by far too quickly; we were genuinely sad to pack our bags this morning. The location strikes a great balance, remaining surprisingly peaceful despite being close to the center. Thick drapes and solid double-glazed windows kept street sounds to an absolute minimum, meaning it was blissfully quiet every evening. Thanks to that tranquility and a supportive mattress, we both slept like rocks throughout the visit. I also had to take a couple of urgent work video calls, and the complimentary Wi-Fi worked flawlessly without dropping once. Warm hospitality, spotless rooms, and true comfort make this an easy recommendation. We're already planning a longer return trip.

The plush mattress and blackout curtains worked wonders, and I slept like a log both nights. Breakfast the next morning was another highlight; the buffet had an impressive spread with a fantastic made-to-order omelet station, fresh tropical fruit, and surprisingly great coffee. It struck the ideal balance between high energy and genuine comfort. We will definitely be back for another stay soon.

Had a lovely weekend stay at the InterContinental. The historic lobby sets the tone right away with all that ornate detailing, yet everything feels well-maintained. Check-in was painless and the front desk clerk happily arranged a slightly late checkout for our Sunday morning. Our room in the historic tower had a ton of character, high ceilings, and a ridiculously comfortable king bed with great pillows. We spent an hour at the indoor pool, which is gorgeous with its vintage tilework--definitely don't skip it if you stay here. Location made walking to dinner and morning coffee ridiculously easy. Only slight minus was a bit of a wait for the elevators during peak morning hours, but otherwise a seamless, relaxing trip. Would book again.

Just got back from a three-night getaway at The James and honestly had a fantastic time. The vibe in the lobby is really cool without feeling overly pretentious, and the front desk staff was super warm right off the bat. Our room was surprisingly quiet considering how close you are to all the action on Rush Street. The bed was ridiculously comfortable--seriously had some of the best sleep I've had in months. Loved the huge shower and the little details, like having a proper coffee setup in the morning instead of the cheap powdered stuff. The elevator wait was slightly slow during the Saturday afternoon rush, but that was really my only minor gripe. Everything else was top notch and we'll definitely be coming back next time we're in town.

We booked a weekend stay at the Knickerbocker on a whim and were genuinely impressed. Right off the bat, the classic architecture and lobby vibe set a great tone. Check-in was painless, and the front desk clerk even managed to get us into our room an hour early, which was a lifesaver after our flight. The room itself had high ceilings, an incredibly comfortable mattress, and decent soundproofing--we barely heard street noise despite the busy area. Housekeeping did a great job keeping everything spotless each morning. The location made walking everywhere super convenient, especially for grabbing dinner and coffee nearby. A solid, hassle-free stay with plenty of charm. Would happily book here again next time we visit.

We had a fantastic weekend at Hotel Monaco. Right from the moment we walked in, the front desk team made us feel welcome, even handing us a glass of wine since we arrived right during the evening happy hour in the lobby. The decor has so much personality--definitely not your typical boring corporate hotel. Our room had a plush window seat overlooking the street that I ended up reading in every morning with my coffee. The bed was super comfortable with great pillows, and the bathroom was spotless with really nice toiletries. Location was ideal for walking to nearby restaurants and catching the train. A really fun, cozy stay, we'd definitely come back.

Had a really lovely weekend at the Omni. Valet was super quick when we pulled up, which set a nice tone right off the bat after a five-hour drive. The lobby smelled amazing and the front desk clerk happily accommodated our request for a higher floor. Our room was spotless and surprisingly quiet given how busy the area was outside; I barely heard a peep from the hallway either. The bed was like sleeping on a cloud, and I appreciate that the blackout curtains actually overlapped properly so the morning sun didn't wake us at dawn. We grabbed breakfast downstairs on Sunday morning--the omelet station was fantastic and the coffee was surprisingly strong. Small perks make a difference, definitely staying here next time.

Honestly loved our weekend at the Palmer House. Walking into that lobby for the first time took my breath away--the ceiling murals and historic chandeliers give it such an old-school glamour vibe. Our room on the 14th floor wasn't massive, but the beds were super plush and we both slept soundly without hearing street noise from Monroe. The bathroom was spotless, though the shower pressure was just average. The location is unbeatable; we literally walked everywhere, from the Art Institute to Millennium Park, in under five minutes. Grabbing a cocktail at the lobby bar was pricey but totally worth it for the people-watching alone. Would definitely rebook next time we visit.

Stayed at the Sheraton for three nights during a weekend trip, and it totally exceeded what I was expecting. Check-in was painless even though the lobby was busy, and the front desk clerk happily gave us an upper floor when we asked. The bed was crazy comfortable--honestly some of the best hotel sleep I've had in ages--and the room stayed surprisingly quiet despite being close to the elevators. Water pressure in the shower was great, which is always a big deal for me. We grabbed breakfast downstairs on Saturday; the buffet was fresh and restocked quickly, though the coffee took a minute to arrive. Location made getting around super easy. Overall, just a really solid, reliable stay with friendly staff. Would definitely book here again.

Had a wonderful weekend getaway at the Sofitel. The French-inspired touches really set this place apart from standard high-end chains. Our room was spotless, whisper-quiet, and that signature bed is genuinely the most comfortable hotel mattress I have ever slept on. Woke up totally refreshed both mornings. The bathroom had fantastic water pressure and lovely Lanvin toiletries that smelled incredible. We grabbed drinks at the bar downstairs on Friday night; the cocktails were top notch, though a bit on the pricier side, which is to be expected. Front desk staff greeted us warmly every time we walked through the lobby. Location made it super easy to walk to great restaurants and shops nearby. Would gladly book here again for our next trip.

We booked a corner room at the Swissotel for a long weekend getaway and were completely blown away by the views. Waking up to the sunrise over Lake Michigan and the river right from our bed was incredible. The triangular shape of the building gives the rooms a really unique, expansive layout. Bed was super plush, and the bathroom had a fantastic soaking tub that my wife loved after a full day of walking around the city. The front desk team was very welcoming, even managed to get us checked in an hour early without any hassle. Location is ideal--quiet enough at night to sleep soundly, but an easy stroll over to the Riverwalk and Millennium Park. The lobby bar was a bit crowded in the evenings, but drinks were great. We'd definitely return.

We booked a weekend trip to Chicago on short notice and ended up picking the Talbott mostly because we wanted to be close to the Gold Coast shops. Honestly, it turned out to be such a great choice. The boutique vibe hits you right when you walk in--very warm, intimate, and quiet compared to the massive chain hotels nearby. Our king room was spotless with high ceilings and an extremely comfortable bed that made it hard to get up in the mornings. The water pressure in the shower was surprisingly strong too, which I always appreciate. Front desk team was super friendly and gave us a fantastic dinner suggestion just around the corner on Rush Street. It's tucked away enough to avoid the crazy street noise, yet you can walk everywhere. Will definitely return.

Stayed at the Affinia for four nights during a trip to the city, and it ended up being an excellent base for us. The location made catching the subway super easy, which saved us a ton of cab fare. What really impressed me was the sheer size of the room--especially having a little kitchenette area with a mini-fridge and microwave, which came in handy for late-night leftovers. The bed was surprisingly plush, and despite being on a lower floor near the street, the ambient noise was barely noticeable once the curtains were drawn. Front desk staff were totally chill and let us stash our heavy luggage for several hours after checkout so we could grab one last lunch. Solid value, would happily rebook next time I'm around.

We picked the Allegro for a long weekend to catch a show in the Loop, and the vibe immediately won us over. It has this fantastic Art Deco flair in the lobby that feels classic without being stuffy. The front desk team was warm and had our keys ready right away. Our king room on the 10th floor was quiet, super clean, and the mattress was surprisingly plush--slept like a rock both nights. We loved having morning coffee downstairs before heading out, and being able to just stroll a couple of blocks to the theater and the river was a massive plus. The bathroom was a bit compact, but the shower pressure made up for it. Would happily book another stay next time we visit.

We booked Hotel Amalfi for a long weekend trip and were genuinely impressed. The River North location can't be beat--we walked to practically every dinner spot and caught a show without needing an Uber once. The room had a warm, boutique feel with dimmable lighting and a surprisingly comfortable mattress that made sleeping in way too easy. I also really appreciated the evening cocktail hour on the floor lounge; it was a relaxing way to unwind with a glass of wine before heading out for the night. Front desk folks were super friendly whenever we passed by, always offering bottles of water. The bathroom could use slightly brighter vanity lights, but that's honestly my only minor critique. Really solid stay overall, would return.

We had such a lovely long weekend at the Hotel Ambassador. It's tucked away in a quieter neighborhood, which was a huge relief after spending the afternoon walking through crowded tourist spots. The vintage aesthetic throughout the building gives it so much character without feeling dated. Our room was spotless, the bed was insanely comfortable, and we had plenty of hot water with great water pressure in the morning. Front desk folks were super friendly and gave us a killer tip for a local bakery just two blocks away. The only small thing was waiting a bit for the elevator during morning rush hour, but honestly everything else was so smooth that we didn't really care. Will definitely be booking here next time we visit.

We stayed at the Fairmont for a long weekend and honestly had a fantastic time. The lobby makes an incredible first impression, but what really won us over was the hospitality. Check-in was breezy, and the front desk clerk happily upgraded us to a higher floor with a stunning park view when we mentioned it was our anniversary. The room itself felt plush and well-maintained; the bed was heaven to sleep on and the bathroom had amazing water pressure, which is rare in older high-rises. We grabbed cocktails downstairs at the lounge on our second night and the bartenders were super friendly and made great drinks. Valet was a bit pricey, but that's pretty standard for the area. Would happily book another stay here next time we're in town.

We just got back from a three-night stay at the Hard Rock and honestly had a blast. The whole music memorabilia vibe is super fun without feeling overly tacky. Check-in was painless, and our room on the 14th floor had a killer view of the city skyline. The bed was surprisingly plush, and whatever soundproofing they have going on works wonders because we never heard our neighbors or hallway chatter. Pool area got pretty lively in the afternoons, but the bartenders kept the drinks flowing quickly so you weren't waiting forever. Loved grabbing a quick breakfast and coffee downstairs in the morning too. It's energetic, the staff treats you well, and you just can't beat the central location. Will definitely return next trip!

Stayed at the Hilton for three nights over the weekend and honestly had a really solid trip. The front desk team was super warm when we arrived late Friday, and they actually managed to get us into a high-floor corner room with a great city view. The bed was incredibly comfortable--slept like a rock every night, which rarely happens for me when traveling. The bathroom was spotless, water pressure in the shower was great, and housekeeping kept everything refreshed without being intrusive. We grabbed breakfast down at the lobby restaurant two mornings in a row; the omelet station and fresh coffee were definitely highlights. Valet parking was slightly pricey, but the staff was prompt retrieving our car. Would happily stay here again.

We booked a suite at Homewood for a long four-day weekend with the kids, and it worked out brilliantly. Having a full fridge and an actual stovetop made feeding everyone breakfast so much easier, plus it saved us quite a bit of money on eating out. Our room was spotless, the beds were very comfy, and the AC was quiet enough that it didn't keep waking me up. The complimentary hot breakfast downstairs had a solid spread--waffles, eggs, decent coffee--and the staff constantly wiped down tables and replenished trays with a smile. Parking was straightforward and safe, and the location was close to everything we wanted to do. It felt more like a cozy mini-apartment than a generic hotel room. We'll definitely choose this place again.

Stayed at the Hyatt for four nights during a conference and honestly had zero complaints. Check-in was a breeze even though there was a small line, and the front desk clerk actually took a minute to point out where the best coffee shop nearby was. The room on the 14th floor had a fantastic city view and was surprisingly quiet given the downtown traffic outside. The bed was super comfortable--firm pillows, crisp sheets, and I slept like a rock. The bathroom had great water pressure which isn't always a given in high-rises. Grabbed a quick bite at the lobby lounge one evening; the flatbread and craft beer were really good, just slightly overpriced. Overall, a smooth, reliable stay and I'd book again.

Booked a weekend stay at the InterContinental to celebrate an anniversary, and it honestly exceeded our expectations. The historic architecture gives the lobby such a grand, classic vibe, yet everything felt well-maintained and comfortable. Our room in the historic tower was surprisingly quiet despite being right in the heart of downtown, and the bed made it hard to wake up early. The real highlight for us was the indoor pool--the 1920s design and intricate tilework are incredible in person, so definitely don't forget your swimsuit. Valet was a bit pricey, but the front desk was super welcoming and gave us a complimentary late checkout without any hassle. We would happily book here again.

Had a lovely weekend stay at the Knickerbocker with my partner. The location right off Michigan Avenue made walking to the lakefront and shopping incredibly easy. You can definitely feel the classic history of the building, but our room was very comfortable with a surprisingly plush mattress and plenty of hot water in the shower. The lobby has a great vintage vibe that feels special the second you walk in. Front desk staff were super welcoming and held our bags before check-in without any fuss so we could grab lunch. It can get a tiny bit noisy from the city street traffic below, but nothing a pair of earplugs didn't fix. Overall, a charming, reliable place to crash in a prime spot. We would gladly book here again on our next trip to town.

We had a fantastic weekend at Hotel Monaco. The quirky boutique vibe caught my attention immediately--lots of bold colors and personality without feeling over the top. The staff at the front desk greeted us warmly and even remembered our names later that evening. Our room was surprisingly quiet considering the central location, and that window seat was my absolute favorite spot to sit with morning coffee and watch the city wake up. The bed was plush and super comfortable, making it hard to get up some mornings. We also made good use of the evening wine reception in the lobby, which was a nice touch to unwind before dinner. It's walking distance to so many great spots. Would happily book another stay here next time we're in town.

We booked a weekend at the Omni for an anniversary trip, and honestly, it exceeded our expectations. The front desk staff greeted us warmly and even sent up a couple of complimentary dessert pastries once they heard we were celebrating. Our room was spotless and surprisingly quiet despite the bustling area outside, plus the bed was ridiculously comfortable. We had breakfast downstairs at the restaurant both mornings--the omelet station is definitely worth waking up for, and the coffee was actually hot and fresh. Valet was quick retrieving our car when we went out exploring, though a bit pricey, which is standard for the area anyway. It was just a really smooth, relaxing stay without any hiccups. We'll definitely return next year.

We booked the Palmer on a whim for a long weekend and honestly loved it. The lobby has this great moody lighting and smelled fantastic the second we walked in. Check-in was breezy, and the front desk guy gave us a great tip on a late-night taco spot around the corner. Our room on the fifth floor was surprisingly quiet given how central the location is. The mattress was firm in a good way, and the water pressure in the shower was top-tier, though they could probably use a few more hooks for towels in the bathroom. We grabbed oat milk lattes from the downstairs cafe every morning before heading out to explore. Not completely spotless--there was some dust behind the nightstand--but overall super comfortable, stylish, and reasonably priced. Would definitely stay again.

Had such a relaxing weekend at Swissotel. Right from check-in, the front desk team was incredibly welcoming and managed to get us into our room a bit early, which was a huge relief after a long morning of traveling. The room itself was spotless, quiet, and had those amazingly plush pillows that make it impossible to get out of bed. We also spent some time at the spa and pool area on the second floor--super clean, tranquil, and not overcrowded at all. Breakfast the next morning was another highlight; the omelet station chef was fast and friendly, and the fresh pastries were dangerous. Location made it effortless to walk around the city center too. Will definitely stay here again next time I'm in town.

Our stay at Hotel Affinia was deeply underwhelming and certainly not worth the price tag. We were placed in a low-floor room where the view was just a grim interior airshaft covered in grime and humming HVAC units. Sleep was nearly impossible because of the constant street noise and paper-thin walls that let in every conversation from the hallway. Things did not improve in the morning; the breakfast buffet was a mess, serving lukewarm, rubbery eggs and stale pastries that looked like they had been sitting out for days. To make matters worse, the Wi-Fi was painfully slow and kept dropping out entirely whenever I tried to load basic web pages for work. Between the racket, terrible amenities, and subpar food, we left feeling exhausted and frustrated. I will not be returning.

I had high hopes for Hotel Allegro given the historic charm, but our weekend stay was a major letdown. The room itself felt dusty and neglected; I found stray hairs on the nightstand and crumbs near the baseboards. The bathroom was uncomfortably cramped, featuring peeling paint around the ceiling and terrible water pressure that made taking a quick shower frustrating. When we pulled back the heavy curtains hoping to see the city skyline, the view was just a bleak interior brick wall covered in HVAC pipes. To top it off, the front desk staff treated every basic question like a massive inconvenience, barely looking up from their screens when we asked for extra towels. The stylish lobby doesn't make up for the poor service and lack of upkeep. We won't be returning.

We had high hopes for the Hotel Amalfi, but our three-night visit felt far too long by the end of the first evening. The bedroom cleanliness was unacceptable; we found thick dust on the bedside tables, stray hairs on the duvet, and the carpet clearly had not been vacuumed recently. Things only got worse in the bathroom, where the shower had black mildew creeping along the tile grout and the water pressure was practically non-existent. Whenever we brought these issues up to the front desk, the staff acted dismissive and thoroughly annoyed rather than trying to assist us. It was an extremely disappointing stay, and we certainly will not be returning.

We booked three nights at the Hotel Ambassador hoping for a charming weekend getaway, but it was thoroughly disappointing. The property simply wasn't worth the hefty price tag. Walking into the room, we were immediately struck by how tired and dated the decor felt--think worn carpet edges, faded upholstery, and scuffed dark wood furniture that desperately needs an overhaul. To make matters worse, our 'city view' amounted to an ugly gravel rooftop covered in noisy industrial air conditioning units. The mattress was so uncomfortably stiff that our long weekend felt far too long by the end of the second night; we actually considered packing up early and driving home. I definitely cannot recommend this place.

I expected much better from the Conrad given the brand's reputation, but this trip was a total letdown. Check-in was cold and dismissive; the front desk staff seemed thoroughly annoyed whenever we asked basic questions. Our room looked okay at first glance, but the cleanliness was lacking--dust coated the nightstands and there was stray hair on the desk chair. The bathroom was even worse, featuring a slow-draining tub, weak water pressure, and visible mildew along the shower grout. To top it off, the walls are paper-thin. We were kept awake half the night by loud conversations in the hallway and traffic noise echoing up from below. For the premium price, the lack of upkeep and poor service are simply unacceptable. I won't be returning.

I expected far more from the Fairmont given the premium rates they charge, but our weekend was a massive letdown. We paid extra for a high-floor room hoping for a scenic skyline view, only to stare directly into a drab concrete parking structure and rooftop HVAC units. To make matters worse, those same mechanical units droned loudly all night, ruining any chance of sleep. The front desk staff seemed thoroughly indifferent when we brought this up; the receptionist barely looked up from her computer and offered a dismissive shrug instead of trying to move us. Nothing about this stay felt worth the steep price tag. Between the noisy room, miserable outlook, and chilly service, we will not be returning.

Our stay at the Hard Rock was a massive letdown from start to finish. Check-in felt like an inconvenience to the front desk staff, who barely made eye contact and offered zero information about the property. When we finally got up to the room, the view was nothing more than an ugly, humming rooftop ventilation unit surrounded by gravel. The bathroom was in desperate need of maintenance--the shower drained at a snail's pace, leaving an inch of standing dirty water around our feet, and the lighting was harsh and flickering. To top it off, getting any decent rest was practically impossible. The mattress was lumpy and rock-hard, and street noise bled right through the thin windows all night long. For the high price tag, this was a thoroughly frustrating experience.
I expected so much more from a brand like Hilton, but this trip was a massive letdown

I was thoroughly let down by my recent stay at the Homewood. For what they charge per night, it simply did not feel worth the price at all. The entire place was shockingly loud; the walls seem paper-thin, so I was constantly disturbed by doors slamming in the hallway and heavy footsteps from the floor above. Because of all the noise and an uncomfortably lumpy mattress, I barely slept a wink the whole weekend. To make matters worse, the wifi was virtually useless. The signal kept dropping every ten minutes, making it impossible to stream a movie or answer basic work emails. I expected a reliable, restful visit, but left feeling exhausted and frustrated. I won't be returning.

Our weekend at the Hyatt fell completely flat. We were placed on a lower floor directly above the loading dock, leaving us staring at a brick wall and a row of overflowing dumpsters instead of any decent skyline. The ambient noise was relentless--trash trucks at 5 AM, loud plumbing in the adjacent walls, and constant thumping from the hallway kept us awake. I barely slept three hours either night on what felt like a sagging, worn-out mattress. Because of the sheer lack of rest and frustrating environment, two nights felt far too long, and we found ourselves wishing we had just checked out early on Sunday morning. For the steep price tag, the complete lack of peace and comfort was totally unacceptable. We won't return.

I had high expectations for the InterContinental, but our weekend here was deeply underwhelming. The entire property feels stuck in the 1990s; the heavy floral drapes and worn wood furniture were desperately dated rather than historic. Cleanliness was also a major letdown, as we spotted thick layers of dust behind the nightstands and strange carpet stains near the closet. The bathroom was the worst part--cramped, poorly lit, with cracked grout lining the tub and water pressure that barely managed a trickle. By the second morning, the environment felt so gloomy that our three-night booking felt far too long, and we genuinely couldn't wait to check out. For the luxury price tag, the subpar quality and lack of upkeep simply aren't justified.

We were really let down by our stay at The James. The only positive aspect was the convenient location, which made walking to nearby restaurants and shops easy, but everything else fell short. When we checked in, the front desk staff treated us like an inconvenience, barely making eye contact and offering zero help with our bags. The room itself was poorly maintained and visibly dirty; thick dust coated the headboard, and the carpet clearly had not been vacuumed properly. The bathroom was the worst part, featuring a slow-draining shower that pooled dirty water around our feet and grime along the tile grout. For the price they charge, the complete lack of basic cleanliness and hospitable service was unacceptable. We won't return.

We had high hopes for our stay at the Knickerbocker, but it turned into a massive letdown. Sleeping here was nearly impossible; between the paper-thin walls carrying noise from the corridor and a sagging, lumpy mattress, I tossed and turned all night. When I looked out the window in the morning, the 'city view' we paid extra for was literally just a grim brick airshaft covered in pigeons. The bathroom felt equally neglected, featuring weak water pressure, stained grout around the tub, and a vanity counter so tiny you could barely rest a toothbrush on it. To make matters worse, the breakfast was dreadful. Everything at the buffet was lukewarm, the scrambled eggs were rubbery and flavorless, and the staff seemed completely indifferent to empty platters. We definitely won't be returning.

I had high hopes for Hotel Monaco, but our two-night stay ended up feeling far too long. The paper-thin walls made it impossible to get any rest; we heard sirens outside, loud hallway chatter, and our neighbor's television blaring all night. In the morning, the breakfast was a major letdown with lukewarm coffee, stale pastries, and rubbery eggs that felt like an afterthought. Given the premium rates and additional hidden fees tacked onto the final bill, this place was simply not worth the price. Between the endless racket and the mediocre food, it was an incredibly disappointing trip, and I won't be returning.

We booked the Omni expecting a high-end weekend, but the whole visit fell completely flat. The bathroom was noticeably outdated, featuring chipped tiles around the baseboard, low water pressure, and a shower drain that backed up within minutes. Opening our curtains revealed a grim view directly into a concrete alley lined with noisy exhaust vents. Trying to catch up on remote work was an exercise in frustration because the in-room wifi constantly disconnected and was far too slow to load basic pages. By Sunday morning, what was supposed to be a relaxing three-night trip felt entirely too long, and we found ourselves eager to pack our bags and head home early. Booked Swissotel expecting reliable luxury, but our weekend was just one annoyance after another. Check-in took forty minutes because the front desk only had two agents handling a massive line, and neither seemed bothered by the wait. The room looked okay at first glance, but the AC had a persistent, high-pitched rattle that kept us up half the night, and housekeeping skipped replenishing the coffee pods and towels on day two. When we called down, nobody answered the service line. Breakfast was another letdown--lukewarm eggs, burnt pastries, and dirty tables everywhere while staff casually chatted in the corner. Definitely not worth the steep room rate. We won't be returning.

I really wanted to love The Talbott because the location near the Gold Coast is fantastic, but our weekend stay was a letdown. Check-in felt cold and rushed, like we were inconveniencing the front desk. Once upstairs, the room itself looked tired. The carpet had a weird musty odor, and the bathroom door didn't even shut properly unless you really forced it. The worst part was the street noise and the thin walls; we could clearly hear the elevator chiming and our neighbors talking all night long, so we barely slept. For the price they charge per night, you expect a boutique luxury vibe, but it felt more like an overpriced, neglected chain hotel. Definitely won't be returning on our next trip to Chicago.
